messages.subject: New TITAN pipeline
messages.body_plain:
Dear User,

There is a new pipeline for running TITAN to perform copy number analysis in whole genome and exome sequencing data.
You can obtain the pipeline from https://github.com/MO-BCCRC/titan_workflow.  This pipeline is based on the KRONOS <https://pypi.python.org/pypi/kronos-pipeliner> workflow (Taghiyar et al, 2016 <http://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2016/02/22/040352.abstract>).
TITANRunner is now deprecated and will not be supported.

I would like to thank Diljot Grewal, Ali Bashashati, and Jafar Taghiyar from the Shah Lab <http://compbio.bccrc.ca> at the BC Cancer Agency for creating this pipeline.

Thank you for your interest in TITAN.

Best,

Gavin Ha, Ph.D.
Postdoctoral Research Fellow
Laboratory of Matthew Meyerson
Dana-Farber Cancer Institute
Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT
415 Main Street, Cambridge, MA 02142
Phone: 617-714-7495

messages.subject: Where can I find the generateMap.pl script?
messages.subject_clean: Where can I find the generateMap.pl script?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gavin,

I am interesting in working with TitanCNA on a non-model pathogen to primarily study gene conversion (LOH) as well as CNVs. Since It is a non-model, I need to generate my own mappability file using the HMMcopy suite.  However, I cannot seem to find the perl script referenced "util/mappability/generateMap.pl > mappability.bw <http://mappability.bw>".

In fact, I'm not entirely sure what this file path even means, is it pointing to a script located in a directly "util" subdirectory "mappability"?  Several other functions, such as "readCounter" are in a similar format.

I am fairly certain HMMcopy is installed correctly, as the help options do appear when i enter "wigsToRangedData" for example, though not "readCounter"

Any help would be appreciated, and apologies for my introductory-level knowledge of R.

Michael

messages.subject: Re: Where can I find the generateMap.pl script?
messages.subject_clean: Where can I find the generateMap.pl script?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

The HMMcopy suite consists of 2 components, an R package and tools to be run from the command line.  Please refer to http://compbio.bccrc.ca/software/hmmcopy/

util and mappability both refer to directories found in zip that can be downloaded here: http://compbio-bccrc.sites.olt.ubc.ca/software/request-to-download?sw=HMMCopy

wigsToRangedData is an R function that can be accessed once the R package is downloaded and installed directly from Bioconductor. This is distinct from the executables (to be run on the command line) such as generateMap.pl and generateMap

Hope this helps.

Best,
Gavin

Hi Gavin,
Unfortunately I am having another error  running the generateMap.pl script.

Submiting:
util/mappability/generateMap.pl /bigdata/judelsonlab/mmatson/projects/refSeqs/pacBio/pacBio_V1.2_5-17-16.fa > data/pacBioMappability.bw

Returns:

No output file specified, writing BigWig file to: /bigdata/judelsonlab/mmatson/projects/refSeqs/pacBio/pacBio_V1.2_5-17-16.fa.map.bw <http://pacBio_V1.2_5-17-16.fa.map.bw>

Command: bowtie --wrapper basic-0 -f -v 0 --quiet /bigdata/judelsonlab/mmatson/projects/refSeqs/pacBio/pacBio_V1.2_5-17-16.fa -

stdin is empty of data

The directory in which I am submitting the command is "/bigdata/judelsonlab/mmatson/projects/geneConversion/titanCNA/HMMcopy" and I am directing the resulting files to the "data" subdirectory.  The (five) Bowtie index files are located in the directory of the reference sequence.

My main question is why the script isn't recognizing the reference sequence as the stdin.

Thanks for the help,
Michael
